Record sheet's grab band stopped at its own header. That sheet pads its top by --obnotion-space-6, four times the menu sheets, so its bar sits 24px down and a band centred on it ran 2..50px from the sheet's top edge while the header starts at 32. Measured consequence: the band answered every press aimed at the title, and both 44px header actions delivered 26px. Main-item cell touch target: tried and reverted, byte-identically. A downward negative-inset pseudo-element to lift the 169x34 cell to the 44px floor is a measured no-op here for two independent reasons — the cell clips its overflow, so the pseudo-element is cut back to the cell box (the last row gained 0px), and in a contiguous table the next row's own area begins exactly where this one's box ends, so there are no dead pixels to reclaim. Only row height reaches 44 and that is a density setting. Reverted rather than shipped, since a rule that measures as a no-op advertises a fix that is not there. Replaced by a check that measures the reach and asserts the property that IS achievable: no press lands on the wrong row.

Taken for a state this packet's own criterion asks about and nothing measured: 'checked, indeterminate, disabled and focus each produce a measurable difference, per family'. The pass built to answer it found the toggle switch reading byte-identical focused and at rest across background, border, image, shadow and opacity — no focus indicator at all, where the three checkbox families each get one from .obnotion-checkbox:focus-visible.

One rule: .obnotion-toggle-switch:focus-visible, the same outline and ring the checkbox carries, because they are the same control to a reader even though they are different shapes. Watched failing by renaming the selector: the family reads 'focus NO'. THE FINDING ALMOST WENT THE OTHER WAY. The first run reported the switch with no checked, indeterminate or focus state, and the cause was the pass reading a signature in the same tick as the state change while the switch's 0.15s background transition was still running — the other three families change background-image, which has no transition, so only one family lied. Transitions are now disabled for that pass. A theme root, a :checked match and a pseudo-element read all had to be ruled out first, and recording it as a product defect would have been a fabricated bug in a shipped control.

One declaration: flex-wrap: wrap on .obnotion-toolbar. The earlier note called the two fixes opposite directions and that was wrong — wrapping is ADDITIVE. flex-wrap does nothing at any width where the row already fits, so 402 and up are untouched by construction, and at 320 the clusters take a second line instead of overhanging. Letting the cluster shrink was the alternative and does not work: it is flex: 0 0 auto with fixed-size icon children and overflow: visible, so shrinking moves the overflow into the cluster rather than removing it. Measured: header descendants past the header's content box 1 -> 0, and back to 1 with the declaration removed.

Taken for a defect the set-equality check this phase asked for found on its first run: the shipped menu row measures 13px inside an owned menu and inside a filter panel, and 16px inside a record-detail sheet. Same component, same class, three containers, two sizes.

One literal fallback: font-size: var(--obnotion-font-md, 13px) on .obnotion-menu-item.obnotion-menu-item. Type tokens live on the plugin's token roots, so a row in a surface mounted outside them resolved the var to nothing, the declaration was dropped entirely, and the row took whatever the host gives a bare button — measured at 14px on a bare page and 16px in the sheet. The switch's radius carries the same fallback for the same reason. TWO THINGS WORTH RECORDING. The fallback was first added to .obnotion-menu-item and changed nothing, because this doubled-specificity rule already owned the property — a shadowed declaration looks exactly like one that did not work. And the existing check for this ('a menu row lays out identically in any sheet') compares min-height, padding and height, all of which the row declares; the one property it did NOT declare is the one that drifted, which is the whole argument for set equality over a spot check. The stylesheet learns depth. A sheet's z-index reads --obnotion-sheet-z-index so a child paints above the surface that opened it instead of tying with it, the scrim reads --obnotion-sheet-scrim-z-index so the single backdrop sits between the top two rather than behind both, and a parent under an open child dims and pulls its content back. That parent rule doubles its marking class: the entrance rule sets opacity 1 at the same two-class weight and sits later in the file, so an equal-weight rule was written and never rendered. Dropdown and relation sheets became flex columns whose option list owns the scrolling, with a mask at the cut, so a long picker keeps its title and close on screen; sheet-presented modals hide the host's own close and let their content box scroll under a shared header.
